name: Bihu
info: A set of three important Assamese festivals marking the agricultural seasons, celebrated with feasts, music, and the energetic Bihu dance.
history: Rooted in ancient agrarian traditions, it brings together all communities of Assam regardless of background.
trivia: Rongali Bihu, celebrated in April, marks the Assamese New Year and is the most colorful of the three.
funFact: During Bihu, the unique 'Pepa' instrument made from a buffalo horn is played, producing an iconic and resonant sound!

name: Durga Puja
info: An annual festival revering the Hindu goddess Durga, celebrating her epic victory over the shape-shifting demon Mahishasura.
history: It gained prominence during the British era when wealthy Bengali landlords organized grand pujas. Today, it's one of the world's largest public arts festivals.
trivia: The grand idols are traditionally crafted using mud from the banks of the river Hooghly.
funFact: In 2021, Kolkata's Durga Puja was officially inscribed on the prestigious UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity!

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
info: A spectacular 10-day festival celebrating the arrival of Lord Ganesha to earth from Mount Kailash.
history: Revitalized by freedom fighter Lokmanya Tilak in 1893 to unite the public and circumvent the British ban on Hindu gatherings.
trivia: Massive clay idols of Ganesha are installed publicly and finally immersed in water bodies on Anant Chaturdashi.
funFact: Mumbai's 'Lalbaugcha Raja' is the most famous idol, drawing millions of devotees who wait in line for over 24 hours just to get a glimpse!

name: Herath (Maha Shivaratri)
info: The most important festival for Kashmiri Pandits, celebrating the wedding of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati.
history: Herath means 'Night of Shiva'. It has unique regional rituals that differ significantly from Shivaratri celebrated elsewhere.
trivia: Walnuts are soaked in water pots symbolizing the deities, and later distributed as the main 'prasad' (offering).
funFact: During Herath, it traditionally snows in Kashmir, which the locals consider an auspicious blessing from Lord Shiva himself!

name: Onam
info: An annual harvest festival and the most important festival of Kerala. It features grand boat races, tiger dances, and a massive feast.
history: Celebrated to honor the legendary, benevolent King Mahabali, whose spirit is said to visit his beloved subjects in Kerala during Onam.
trivia: The grand Onam feast, known as 'Onasadya', is a massive vegetarian banquet consisting of over 26 distinct dishes served on a single banana leaf.
funFact: The spectacular 'Vallam Kali' (snake boat race) held during Onam involves beautiful boats that are over 100 feet long, rowed by over 100 oarsmen simultaneously!

name: Pongal
info: A four-day harvest festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya), celebrating the abundance of the harvest.
history: Dating back to the Sangam Age (200 BC to 300 AD), it is one of the oldest continuous festivals in India.
trivia: The festival is named after the traditional dish 'Pongal' (sweetened boiled rice), which means 'to boil over'.
funFact: When the Pongal dish boils over the pot, families joyously shout 'Pongalo Pongal!' symbolizing prosperity overflowing in their homes!

name: Shigmo
info: A massive spring festival in Goa celebrating the harvest and honoring the local warriors returning from battle.
history: While Goa is famous for its Carnival, Shigmo is its deep-rooted traditional Hindu equivalent, blending folk culture with mythology.
trivia: It involves massive, vibrant parades in the streets with people performing traditional folk dances like Ghode Modni and Fugdi.
funFact: During Shigmo, entire villages participate in painting intricate, massive mythological floats that look like they belong in a fantasy movie!

name: Teej
info: A vibrant festival celebrated primarily by women, marking the onset of the monsoon and the union of Lord Shiva and Parvati.
history: It revolves around the folklore that Parvati fasted and prayed for 108 lifetimes to finally be accepted by Lord Shiva.
trivia: Women dress in bright green attire, apply intricate mehndi (henna), and joyously swing on decorated swings hung from large trees.
funFact: A special sweet called 'Ghevar' is exclusively prepared and devoured during this season across Rajasthan!

name: Vaisakhi
info: A historic spring harvest festival that also marks the Sikh New Year and the founding of the Khalsa Panth.
history: In 1699, Guru Gobind Singh chose this harvest festival to establish the Khalsa, transforming the Sikh community.
trivia: Farmers celebrate by performing the energetic Bhangra dance in the fields to express their joy over the golden wheat harvest.
funFact: Nagar Kirtans (street processions) held on Vaisakhi are led by five traditionally dressed Sikhs carrying swords, representing the original 'Panj Pyare' (Beloved Five)!
